title: "Handling zeros in catch and survey observations"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tinyAM)
tinyAM:::.require_tweedie()

guide_root <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT")
source_files <- if (nzchar(guide_root)) {
  c(file.path("R", list.files(file.path(guide_root, "R"), "[.]R$")), "NAMESPACE")
} else {
  list.files(system.file("R", package = "tinyAM"), full.names = TRUE)
}
source_hashes <- tools::md5sum(if (nzchar(guide_root)) {
  file.path(guide_root, source_files)
} else source_files)
versions <- c(tinyAM = as.character(packageVersion("tinyAM")),
  R = as.character(getRversion()), RTMB = as.character(packageVersion("RTMB")),
  mgcv = as.character(packageVersion("mgcv")),
  tweedie = as.character(packageVersion("tweedie")))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  cache.extra = list(versions = versions, sources = unname(source_hashes), inputs = cod_obs))
```

When fish are scarce, a catch or survey sample can record zero for an age
even if fish of that age are present. Positive-only families, including
lognormal (the default), Gamma, and generalized gamma, use only positive
observations in the likelihood. Delta and Tweedie families also use sampled
zeros.

## Observation models that include sampled zeros

Let \(Y_i\) be a recorded catch or survey index for an age and year, and let
\(\widetilde{Y}_i\) be its prediction from the population model. The catch
prediction comes from the Baranov catch equation. The survey prediction is
abundance at sampling time scaled by catchability.

### Delta observations

Delta models describe whether a sample records any fish and how much it
records when fish are observed (Stefánsson 1996). In tinyAM, both parts use
the same predicted catch or survey index, \(\widetilde{Y}_i\). This
prediction is the arithmetic mean across zeros and positives.

Each fleet or survey \(j\) has a soft detection scale
\(\widetilde{Y}_{50,j}\), the predicted catch or index at which half of
observations are expected to be zero. The prediction and the scale use the
observation's units. Let \(r_i=\widetilde{Y}_i/\widetilde{Y}_{50,j}\) be
the prediction relative to that scale.

The logit link makes \(r_i\) the odds of recording a positive. The
Poisson link gives the chance of at least one event under a Poisson model
with encounter rate \(\lambda_i=\log(2)\,r_i\) (Thorson 2018).

\[
p_{+,i}=\Pr(Y_i>0)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{r_i}{1+r_i}, & \text{logit link},\\[4pt]
1-e^{-\lambda_i}, & \text{Poisson link}.
\end{cases}
\]

The Poisson-link case is equivalent to a complementary log-log (cloglog)
link. The probability of zero is \(p_{0,i}=\Pr(Y_i=0)=1-p_{+,i}\). At
twice the soft detection scale, it is one-third with the logit link and
one-quarter with the Poisson link. See also the
[sdmTMB model description](https://sdmtmb.github.io/sdmTMB/articles/model-description.html#delta-models)
for delta models with two predictors.

```{r encounter-curves, echo=FALSE}
relative <- seq(0, 4, length.out = 161)
curves <- data.frame(relative_prediction = rep(relative, 2),
  probability = c(1 / (1 + relative), exp(-log(2) * relative)),
  family = rep(c("Logit-link delta", "Poisson-link delta"), each = length(relative)))
plotly::plot_ly(curves, x = ~relative_prediction, y = ~probability,
  color = ~family, colors = tam_pal(2), type = "scatter", mode = "lines",
  height = 330,
  hovertemplate = "Prediction / soft detection scale: %{x:.2f}<br>Probability of zero: %{y:.1%}<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>") |>
  plotly::layout(xaxis = list(title = "Prediction / soft detection scale"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Probability of zero", range = c(0, 1), tickformat = ".0%"),
    legend = list(x = 1, y = 1, xanchor = "right", yanchor = "top"))
```

The horizontal scale compares predictions relative to the same soft
detection scale. At large predictions, Poisson-link delta gives a lower
probability of zero.

For either delta option, the positive component has arithmetic mean

\[
m_{+,i}=\frac{\widetilde{Y}_i}{p_{+,i}},
\qquad
p_{+,i}\,m_{+,i}=\widetilde{Y}_i.
\]

Only the positives contribute to the overall mean. If the predicted catch
is 10 and one quarter of samples are positive, the positives must average
40 so that \(0.25\times40=10\). The positive distribution can be lognormal,
Gamma, or generalized gamma. For example, delta lognormal uses

\[
\log Y_i\mid Y_i>0
\sim N\!\left(\log m_{+,i}-\frac{\sigma_i^2}{2},\ \sigma_i^2\right).
\]

Here \(\sigma_i\) controls the spread on the log scale. Subtracting
\(\sigma_i^2/2\) makes \(m_{+,i}\) the arithmetic mean of the positives.
The default ordinary lognormal family uses the assessment prediction as its
conditional median.

A sampled zero contributes its log probability. A positive contributes the
log probability of a positive plus its log density. Writing \(g_{+,i}\)
for the positive density on the log-observation scale gives

\[
\ell_i=
\begin{cases}
\log p_{0,i}, & Y_i=0,\\[4pt]
\log p_{+,i}+\log g_{+,i}(\log Y_i), & Y_i>0.
\end{cases}
\]

The overall assessment prediction uses a log link. `q_link` independently
controls how the survey formula maps to catchability.

### Tweedie observations

Tweedie models zeros and positive observations through a single
distribution. With power \(1<p_j<2\), it describes a sum of a
Poisson-distributed number of positive Gamma amounts. The sum is zero when
there are no amounts to add (Foster and Bravington 2013).

The variance and probability of zero depend on the predicted arithmetic
mean \(\widetilde{Y}_i\), dispersion \(\phi_i\), and the series' power \(p_j\).

\[
\operatorname{Var}(Y_i)=\phi_i\widetilde{Y}_i^{\,p_j},
\qquad
\Pr(Y_i=0)=
\exp\!\left[-\frac{\widetilde{Y}_i^{\,2-p_j}}{\phi_i(2-p_j)}\right].
\]

The model estimates power separately for each series unless `power` is
supplied. The same dispersion and power govern the probability of zero and
the spread of the positives.

A sampled zero contributes \(\log\Pr(Y_i=0)\). A positive contributes
\(\log f_{\mathrm{Tw}}(Y_i)+\log Y_i\), where \(f_{\mathrm{Tw}}\) is the
Tweedie density for positive values on the original observation scale. It
already includes the probability of recording a positive. The \(\log Y_i\)
term converts the density to the log-observation scale used in the
likelihood. See the
[observation family reference](../reference/observation_families.html)
for dispersion conventions, restrictions, and the alternative positive
families.

## Apply the families to Northern cod

```{r zero-counts, include=FALSE}
years <- 1983:2025
ages <- 2:20
zero_count <- function(x) sum(x$obs == 0 & x$year %in% years & x$age %in% ages,
  na.rm = TRUE)
```

Northern cod has **`r zero_count(cod_obs$catch)` recorded catch zeros** and
**`r zero_count(cod_obs$index)` Fall 2J3KL survey zeros** at ages 2–20+ in
1983–2025. Four fits use the same NCAM-inspired population model and differ
in their catch and survey observation families.

```{r fits, cache=TRUE, results="hide", warning=FALSE}
ncam <- fit_tam(cod_obs, years = 1983:2025, ages = 2:20,
  N_settings = list(process = "off", init = "exp"),
  R_settings = list(process = "rw"),
  F_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_form = ~ 1, mean_ages = 5:14),
  M_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_supplied = ~ I(0.3),
    age_breaks = c(2, 5, 8, 21), mean_ages = 5:14),
  catch_settings = list(sd_form = ~ 1),
  index_settings = list(sd_form = ~ 1, q_form = ~ mono(q_block)),
  silent = TRUE
)

ncam_delta <- update(ncam,
  catch_settings = list(family = delta_lognormal(type = "logit-link")),
  index_settings = list(family = delta_lognormal(type = "logit-link")),
  silent = TRUE
)

ncam_poisson <- update(ncam,
  catch_settings = list(family = delta_lognormal(type = "poisson-link")),
  index_settings = list(family = delta_lognormal(type = "poisson-link")),
  silent = TRUE
)

ncam_tweedie <- update(ncam,
  catch_settings = list(family = tweedie()),
  index_settings = list(family = tweedie()),
  start_par = ncam,
  silent = TRUE
)
```

The ordinary lognormal likelihood excludes the recorded zeros. Delta and
Tweedie likelihoods use them. Missing observations contribute to none of
the likelihoods. The ordinary lognormal prediction is a median, while the
other three predictions are arithmetic means across zeros and positives.
The Tweedie fit uses the lognormal fit to initialize shared parameters.

```{r fitted-models, include=FALSE, error=FALSE}
fits <- list(Lognormal = ncam, `Logit-link delta` = ncam_delta,
  `Poisson-link delta` = ncam_poisson, Tweedie = ncam_tweedie)
failed <- names(fits)[!vapply(fits, function(fit) isTRUE(fit$is_converged), logical(1))]
if (length(failed)) {
  stop("Northern cod fits failed numerical checks: ", paste(failed, collapse = ", "),
    ". Inspect check_tam() before publishing the comparison.", call. = FALSE)
}
zero_fits <- fits[-1L]
```

### Detection and distribution parameters

```{r detection-scales, echo=FALSE}
parameters <- lapply(fits, function(fit) {
  subset(fit$fixed_par, par %in% c("y50_catch", "y50_index",
    "tweedie_power_catch", "tweedie_power_index"))
})
parameters <- stack_list(parameters, label = "model")
if (nrow(parameters)) {
  parameters$par <- paste0("`", parameters$par, "`")
  knitr::kable(parameters[c("model", "par", "est", "lwr", "upr", "unit")],
    format = "pipe", digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
    col.names = c("Model", "Parameter", "Estimate", "Lower 95%", "Upper 95%", "Units"))
}
```

### Which observations are likely to be zero? {.tabset}

The numbers in each cell are observed thousands of fish. Colour gives the
probability of zero calculated from the selected model. Grey cells mark
missing observations. Hover shows the recorded value, fitted mean, and
probability. Small positives stay distinct from zero. In the labels,
`k` means one thousand of the displayed units.

```{r observation-matrices, include=FALSE}
observations <- lapply(zero_fits, tidy_obs_pred)
observation_matrix <- function(data) {
  cells <- expand.grid(year = years, age = ages)
  key <- match(paste(cells$year, cells$age), paste(data$year, data$age))
  observed <- data$obs[key]
  predicted <- data$pred_mean[key]
  probability <- ifelse(is.na(observed), NA_real_, data$p_zero[key])
  number <- function(x) format(x, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE, digits = 12)
  rounded <- ifelse(observed < 10, formatC(observed, format = "f", digits = 1),
    ifelse(observed < 10000, as.character(round(observed)),
      paste0(round(observed / 1000), "k")))
  cells$label <- ifelse(is.na(observed), "\u2013",
    ifelse(observed == 0, "0", ifelse(observed < 0.1, "<0.1", rounded)))
  age_labels <- as.character(ages)
  age_labels[length(ages)] <- paste0(max(ages), "+")
  age_label <- age_labels[match(cells$age, ages)]
  fitted_values <- paste0("<br>Fitted mean: ", number(predicted),
    " thousand fish<br>Probability of zero: ", sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * probability))
  hover <- paste0("Year: ", cells$year, "<br>Age: ", age_label, "<br>",
    ifelse(is.na(observed), "Observation: missing",
      paste0("Observed: ", number(observed), " thousand fish", fitted_values)))
  cells$dark <- !is.na(probability) & probability >= 0.65
  color_scale <- list(c(0, "#f8fbfd"), c(0.5, "#aacdde"), c(1, "#244f67"))
  p <- plotly::plot_ly(x = ages, y = years,
    z = matrix(probability, nrow = length(years)),
    text = matrix(hover, nrow = length(years)),
    type = "heatmap", colorscale = color_scale, zmin = 0, zmax = 1,
    xgap = 1, ygap = 1, hoverinfo = "text", hoverongaps = FALSE,
    colorbar = list(title = list(text = "Probability<br>of zero"), tickformat = ".0%"),
    height = 850)
  for (on_dark in c(FALSE, TRUE)) {
    p <- plotly::add_text(p, data = cells[cells$dark == on_dark, ],
      x = ~age, y = ~year, text = ~label, hovertext = hover[cells$dark == on_dark],
      hoverinfo = "text", textposition = "middle center", showlegend = FALSE,
      textfont = list(size = 10, color = if (on_dark) "white" else "#15252d"),
      inherit = FALSE)
  }
  p <- plotly::layout(p, margin = list(t = 70), plot_bgcolor = "#e3e5e8",
    xaxis = list(title = "Age", side = "top", tickvals = ages, ticktext = age_labels,
      showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, automargin = TRUE),
    yaxis = list(title = "Year", range = c(max(years) + .5, min(years) - .5),
      tickvals = c(1983, seq(1985, 2025, by = 5)), showgrid = FALSE))
  p <- htmlwidgets::onRender(p, "function(el) {
    function resize() {
      window.requestAnimationFrame(function() {
        if (el.offsetWidth > 0 && el._fullLayout && window.Plotly) {
          window.Plotly.Plots.resize(el);
        }
      });
    }
    document.addEventListener('shown.bs.tab', resize);
    if (window.jQuery) window.jQuery(document).on('shown.bs.tab', resize);
    window.addEventListener('resize', resize);
  }")
  htmltools::div(style = "overflow-x: auto;",
    htmltools::div(style = "min-width: 865px;", plotly::config(p, displayModeBar = FALSE)))
}
observation_matrix_tabs <- function(type) {
  ids <- paste0("observation-matrix-", type, "-", seq_along(observations))
  tabs <- lapply(seq_along(observations), function(i) {
    htmltools::tags$button(names(observations)[i], type = "button",
      class = "tinyam-matrix-tab", id = paste0(ids[i], "-tab"), role = "tab",
      `aria-controls` = ids[i], `aria-selected` = if (i == 1L) "true" else "false",
      tabindex = if (i == 1L) "0" else "-1")
  })
  panels <- lapply(seq_along(observations), function(i) {
    htmltools::div(class = "tinyam-matrix-panel", hidden = if (i == 1L) NULL else "hidden",
      id = ids[i], role = "tabpanel", `aria-labelledby` = paste0(ids[i], "-tab"),
      tabindex = "0", observation_matrix(observations[[i]][[type]]))
  })
  controller <- "(function() {
    var root = document.currentScript.parentElement;
    var tabs = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll('.tinyam-matrix-tab'));
    var panels = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll('.tinyam-matrix-panel'));
    function resize() {
      window.requestAnimationFrame(function() {
        panels.filter(function(p) { return !p.hidden; }).forEach(function(panel) {
          panel.querySelectorAll('.plotly').forEach(function(plot) {
            if (plot.offsetWidth > 0 && plot._fullLayout && window.Plotly) {
              window.Plotly.Plots.resize(plot);
            }
          });
        });
      });
    }
    function select(index, focus) {
      tabs.forEach(function(tab, i) {
        tab.setAttribute('aria-selected', String(i === index));
        tab.tabIndex = i === index ? 0 : -1;
        panels[i].hidden = i !== index;
      });
      if (focus) tabs[index].focus();
      resize();
    }
    tabs.forEach(function(tab, index) {
      tab.addEventListener('click', function() { select(index, false); });
      tab.addEventListener('keydown', function(event) {
        var next = {ArrowLeft: (index + tabs.length - 1) % tabs.length,
          ArrowRight: (index + 1) % tabs.length, Home: 0, End: tabs.length - 1}[event.key];
        if (next === undefined) return;
        event.preventDefault();
        event.stopPropagation();
        select(next, true);
      });
    });
    if (window.ResizeObserver) {
      var width = 0;
      new ResizeObserver(function(entries) {
        var next = entries[0].contentRect.width;
        if (next !== width) { width = next; if (width > 0) resize(); }
      }).observe(root);
    }
  }());"
  style <- ".tinyam-matrix-tablist { display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:.2rem;
    border-bottom:1px solid #adc3cc; margin-bottom:.5rem; }
    .tinyam-matrix-tab { font:inherit; color:inherit; cursor:pointer; background:transparent;
      padding:.45rem .7rem; border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:.25rem .25rem 0 0; }
    .tinyam-matrix-tab[aria-selected=true] { color:#003e56; background:#edf4f7; border-color:#adc3cc; }
    .tinyam-matrix-tab:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #003e56; outline-offset:2px; }
    .tinyam-matrix-panel[hidden] { display:none !important; }"
  htmltools::div(class = "tinyam-matrix-tabs", id = paste0("observation-matrix-", type, "-tabs"),
    htmltools::tags$style(htmltools::HTML(style)),
    htmltools::div(class = "tinyam-matrix-tablist", role = "tablist",
      `aria-label` = paste(type, "observation family"), tabs),
    htmltools::div(class = "tinyam-matrix-panels", panels),
    htmltools::tags$script(htmltools::HTML(controller)))
}
```

### Number of zeros {.tabset}

For each year, dots count the recorded zeros and lines sum each model's
fitted probabilities of zero across the same sampled ages. For example, three
ages with probabilities of 0.2, 0.5, and 0.8 contribute 1.5 expected zeros.
Both counts use sampled observations with a fitted probability and exclude
structural zeros. Years without eligible observations leave a gap.

```{r annual-zero-counts, include=FALSE}
zero_counts <- lapply(c("catch", "index"), function(type) {
  stack_list(lapply(observations, function(d) {
    tinyAM:::.annual_zero_counts(d[[type]], years = years)
  }), label = "model")
})
names(zero_counts) <- c("catch", "index")
```

#### Catch {#catch-zero-counts}

```{r catch-zero-counts, echo=FALSE}
tinyAM:::.plot_annual_zeros(zero_counts$catch, height = 320)
```

#### Index {#index-zero-counts}

```{r index-zero-counts, echo=FALSE}
tinyAM:::.plot_annual_zeros(zero_counts$index, height = 320)
```

## Compare the assessments

Only six catches and two survey observations are positive at age 20+.
The terminal abundance estimates therefore draw heavily on the fitted
population dynamics. Shading marks the low-stock years from 1992 to 2010.

```{r trajectories, echo=FALSE}
terminal <- stack_list(lapply(fits, function(fit) subset(fit$pop$N, age == 20)),
  label = "model")
ssb <- do.call(get_ssb, fits)
low_stock <- list(type = "rect", xref = "x", yref = "paper",
  x0 = 1992, x1 = 2010, y0 = 0, y1 = 1, layer = "below",
  fillcolor = "rgba(170,205,222,0.3)", line = list(width = 0))
plot_trend(terminal, color = ~model, colors = tam_pal(4),
  ylab = "Age 20+ abundance (thousands of fish)", add_buttons = FALSE,
  add_intervals = FALSE) |>
  plotly::layout(shapes = list(low_stock),
    yaxis = list(type = "log", range = log10(range(terminal$est) * c(0.8, 1.2))))
plot_trend(ssb, color = ~model, colors = tam_pal(4),
  ylab = "Spawning biomass (tonnes)")
```

These differences describe sensitivity to the observation family.
Inspect numerical checks and residual diagnostics alongside the trajectories
in the [Northern cod dashboard](../examples/northern-cod-zeros/index.html).

## Forecast held-out observations

For each target year from 2006 to 2025, hindcasts fit through the previous
year and forecast one year with terminal F held constant. The same 20
folds are attempted for every family.

```{r hindcasts, cache=TRUE, dependson="fits", warning=FALSE}
hind <- fit_hindcast(ncam, ncam_delta, ncam_poisson, ncam_tweedie,
  folds = 20, proj_settings = list(F_mult = 1))
```

```{r hindcast-coverage, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
forecast_folds <- subset(hind$fold_diagnostics, !is_reference)
n_failed <- sum(!forecast_folds$is_converged)
if (n_failed) {
  cat(sprintf("%d of %d forecast fits failed. The scores below use only matched forecasts.\n",
    n_failed, nrow(forecast_folds)))
}
```

All four models are scored on the same held-out positive survey
observations. Scores compare predicted medians with observations on
the log scale, so a twofold overprediction and a twofold underprediction
count equally. Log-RMSE gives large misses more weight. MASE compares
mean absolute log error with a simple forecast that carries forward the
last available positive observation. Lower scores are better, and a MASE
below one shows that the model beats that benchmark (Carvalho et al. 2021).

```{r hindcast-scores, echo=FALSE}
survey <- hind$forecast_pairs$index
survey$log_prediction <- ifelse(survey$model == "ncam",
  log(survey$pred), survey$log_pred_positive)
survey <- subset(survey, is.finite(obs) & obs > 0 & is.finite(log_prediction))
key <- with(survey, interaction(fold, year, age, survey, drop = TRUE))
support <- split(survey$model, key)
common <- names(support)[vapply(support, function(x) {
  length(x) == length(fits) && length(unique(x)) == length(fits)
}, logical(1))]
matched <- survey[as.character(key) %in% common, ]
labels <- c(ncam = "Lognormal", ncam_delta = "Logit-link delta",
  ncam_poisson = "Poisson-link delta", ncam_tweedie = "Tweedie")
scores <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(labels), function(model_name) {
  d <- subset(matched, model == model_name)
  data.frame(Model = labels[[model_name]], Cases = nrow(d),
    `Log-RMSE` = if (nrow(d)) compute_hindcast_rmse(d) else NA_real_,
    MASE = if (nrow(d)) compute_hindcast_mase(d) else NA_real_, check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(scores, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

The true stock history is unknown, so these scores compare one-year
forecasts of observed survey indices. On the matched positive records,
Poisson-link delta had the lowest log-RMSE and MASE.

Brier scores were also calculated to compare forecasts of whether a
held-out catch or survey observation would be zero. The score averages the
squared difference between the forecast probability of zero and the
outcome, coded as one for a zero and zero for a positive. Lower is better,
and a score of zero indicates perfect forecasts on those records. The
three models are scored on the same held-out observations.

```{r hindcast-zero-scores, echo=FALSE}
occurrence <- hind$forecast_pairs$occurrence
if (NROW(occurrence)) {
  keys <- intersect(c("type", "fold", "horizon", "year", "age", "survey", "fleet"), names(occurrence))
  case <- do.call(paste, c(occurrence[keys], sep = "\r"))
  support <- split(occurrence$model, case)
  common <- names(support)[vapply(support, function(x) {
    length(x) == length(zero_fits) && length(unique(x)) == length(zero_fits)
  }, logical(1))]
  occurrence <- occurrence[case %in% common, ]
}
if (NROW(occurrence)) {
  groups <- split(occurrence, interaction(occurrence$model, occurrence$type, drop = TRUE))
  brier <- do.call(rbind, lapply(groups, function(x) {
    data.frame(Model = unname(labels[x$model[1L]]), Observations = x$type[1L],
      Cases = nrow(x), Brier = mean(x$brier))
  }))
  knitr::kable(brier, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No zero observations or positives were available on common forecast cases.\n")
}
```

Poisson-link delta had the lowest Brier score for catch. It matched Tweedie
for the survey index at the precision shown. The Brier scores assess
forecasts for individual observations. For agreement in annual totals,
see the [number of zeros plots](#number-of-zeros).

## Compare information criteria

Marginal AIC averages the likelihood over the model's random effects.
Conditional AIC (cAIC) evaluates how well each model would predict repeat
observations from the same underlying stock history. Both account for
model complexity, and lower values are better.

```{r information-criteria, warning=FALSE}
marginal <- AIC(ncam_delta, ncam_poisson, ncam_tweedie)
conditional <- cAIC(ncam_delta, ncam_poisson, ncam_tweedie)
```

```{r information-criteria-table, echo=FALSE}
criteria <- data.frame(Model = names(zero_fits), AIC = marginal$AIC,
  cAIC = conditional[rownames(marginal), "cAIC"])
best_aic <- criteria$Model[which.min(criteria$AIC)]
best_caic <- criteria$Model[which.min(criteria$cAIC)]
criterion_result <- if (identical(best_aic, best_caic)) {
  paste(best_aic, "has the lowest AIC and cAIC.")
} else {
  paste(best_aic, "has the lowest AIC and", best_caic, "has the lowest cAIC.")
}
knitr::kable(criteria, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE)
```

The lognormal model is excluded because it treats sampled zeros as
missing and therefore uses different observations. All three fits have
parameters at their bounds, so the criteria are approximate.
`r criterion_result`

of ecological non-negative continuous data. *Environmental and Ecological
Statistics*, 20, 533–552.
[doi:10.1007/s10651-012-0233-0](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10651-012-0233-0).

Stefánsson, G. 1996. Analysis of groundfish survey abundance data: combining
the GLM and delta approaches. *ICES Journal of Marine Science*, 53(3), 577–588.
[doi:10.1006/jmsc.1996.0079](https://doi.org/10.1006/jmsc.1996.0079).

Thorson, J. T. 2018. Three problems with the conventional delta-model for
biomass sampling data, and a computationally efficient alternative.
*Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences*, 75(9), 1369–1382.
[doi:10.1139/cjfas-2017-0266](https://doi.org/10.1139/cjfas-2017-0266).

```{r dashboard-export, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
dashboard_cache <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_ZEROS_GUIDE_FITS")
if (nzchar(dashboard_cache)) {
  if (!nzchar(guide_root)) stop("Set TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT to the checkout when exporting guide fits.")
  dir.create(dirname(dashboard_cache), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(models = fits, inputs = cod_obs, versions = versions,
    sources = setNames(unname(source_hashes), source_files),
    background = paste(
      "### Northern cod observation families",
      "These NCAM-inspired fits use 1983–2025 and ages 2–20+. Four fits compare ordinary lognormal, logit-link delta lognormal, Poisson-link delta lognormal, and Tweedie catch and survey observations.",
      "See the [handling zeros guide](../../articles/handling-zeros.html) for the equations and fitted distribution parameters.",
      sep = "\n\n")), dashboard_cache)
}
```
